name: Liver
kicker: The body’s detox and metabolism hub · Can regrow itself when damaged
dates: Weighs about 3 pounds in an adult
briefing: The liver is the largest internal organ in the human body, a reddish-brown wedge tucked beneath the right ribs that filters toxins like alcohol straight out of the bloodstream. Its Kupffer cells gobble up worn-out red blood cells, while the greenish fluid it makes, bile, helps the gut digest fat. Heavy drinking can scar it into cirrhosis, but it’s also the only internal organ able to regrow a damaged section.

tossups.p: Ito cells tucked inside this organ store reserves of vitamin A beneath its sinusoidal lining. A dual blood supply feeds it: the hepatic artery brings oxygen-rich blood while a second vessel delivers nutrient-rich blood straight from the intestines and spleen.
tossups.r: Leftover nitrogen from broken-down proteins is turned into urea here before the kidneys remove it. For 10 points, name this organ that stores sugar as glycogen and produces bile to help digest fat.

tossups.p: The Cori cycle ends in this organ, which rebuilds lactic acid made by working muscles back into usable glucose. Peroxisomes inside this organ help break down fatty acids, and its cells manufacture the enzyme glucokinase for aerobic respiration.
tossups.r: Though it looks two-lobed from the front, this organ is technically split into four lobes, including a caudate and a quadrate lobe. For 10 points, name this organ whose Kupffer cells destroy worn-out red blood cells.

tossups.p: This organ is the main site of gluconeogenesis, building new glucose out of non-sugar starting materials. Albumin and most of the body’s blood-clotting proteins are manufactured here as well.
tossups.r: The falciform ligament attaches this organ to the abdominal wall. Heavy drinking can scar this organ into a condition called cirrhosis. For 10 points, name this organ, the largest internal organ in the human body.

tossups.p: A dual blood supply reaches this organ, receiving oxygen-rich blood through the hepatic artery and nutrient-rich blood through a portal vessel coming from the intestines and spleen. It sits directly beneath the diaphragm on the body’s right side.
tossups.r: This organ’s Kupffer cells break down old red blood cells, releasing the pigment bilirubin; when this organ cannot process enough of that pigment, skin can turn yellow with jaundice. For 10 points, name this organ that produces bile for digesting fat.

tossups.p: Vitamin A is stored by this organ’s Ito cells, tucked just beneath its sinusoidal lining. This organ’s cells also make glucokinase, an enzyme used in aerobic respiration, and this organ contains unusually large numbers of peroxisomes.

tossups.p: This organ converts leftover nitrogen from protein breakdown into urea for the kidneys to excrete. The Cori cycle sends lactic acid from tired muscles to this organ, which rebuilds it into glucose.

clues.t: The largest internal organ in the human body, found in the upper right side of the abdomen
Filters toxins such as alcohol out of the bloodstream
Produces bile, a fluid stored in the gallbladder that helps digest fats
Heavy alcohol use can scar it into a disease called cirrhosis
The only internal organ in the human body that can regrow a damaged section
Kupffer cells inside it break down old, worn-out red blood cells
Receives nutrient-rich, oxygen-poor blood from the intestines and spleen through the portal vein
Failing to break down the pigment bilirubin can turn skin yellow, a condition called jaundice
Can become inflamed in a condition called hepatitis
Stores extra sugar as glycogen and releases it back as glucose when the body needs energy
The falciform ligament attaches it to the wall of the abdomen and separates it into lobes
Sits directly beneath the diaphragm, mostly on the body’s right side
Also considered the body’s largest gland, since it releases bile into the digestive tract
The Cori cycle carries lactic acid made by working muscles here, where it’s rebuilt into glucose
Ito cells inside it store vitamin A beneath its lining of blood vessels
Contains large numbers of peroxisomes, organelles that help break down fatty acids
Its cells produce the enzyme glucokinase, used in aerobic respiration
The main site of gluconeogenesis, the process of making new glucose from non-sugar sources
Converts leftover nitrogen from broken-down proteins into urea for the kidneys to remove
Receives a dual blood supply: oxygen-rich blood from the hepatic artery and nutrient-rich blood from the portal vein
Produces most of the body’s blood-clotting proteins, plus albumin, the most common protein in blood plasma
Though it looks like two lobes from the front, it actually has four lobes: right, left, caudate, and quadrate

trap.title: Liver, or kidneys?
trap.body: Both of these organs clean the blood, so clues about “filtering” or “toxins” can point to either one. But bile, Kupffer cells, cirrhosis, glycogen storage, and the portal vein all belong to this organ; urine, nephrons, and the renal pelvis belong to the kidneys instead.
trap.fix: If the clue mentions bile, the gallbladder, jaundice, or alcohol damage, it’s safely this organ; if it mentions urine or filtering waste out of the blood into a liquid, think kidneys instead.
